operations.comment: ; Bases Loaded II: Second Season (NES, MMC1) - commented disassembly (round 5 commentary)
; Memory model: MMC1 PRG mode 2.  Bank 0 is fixed at $8000-$BFFF (engine, NMI, math, ball
; physics, fielding AI); banks 1-15 are switched into $C000-$FFFF.  Code in a switchable bank
; is entered through FarCallBank using that bank's entry table at $C03F.  Every bank starts
; with a copy of the reset stub and ends with a bank-ID byte ($FFDF) and the vectors.
; Bank roles (from their entry points; see each routine's comment):
;   1  umpire voice player + DMC voice samples      9  field-view scroller (second field set)
;   2  front end: title, menus, lineup, scoreboard  10 field reset, second voice-sample set
;   3  screen loader (layouts, palettes, text)      11 batted-ball physics, CPU virtual pad
;   4  password, cutscene scripts, ending           12 runner sprites, camera, sound driver
;   5  metasprite library, play clock, schedule     13 batter/pitcher animation, at-bat end
;   6  CPU fielding and base-running AI             14 pitch close-up sprites
;   7  pitching-screen loader and panels            15 gameplay state machine (PlayState),
;   8  field-view scroller and map blocks              runners, fielders, play judgment
; Conventions: D_Bnn_ADDR / C_Bnn_ADDR are address-based labels on table bytes read by code
; (in data and code regions respectively) whose exact role is open; '@' labels are local
; branch targets.  Names ending _XXXX or _<role> are internal entry points of the routine
; named before them.  Region headers ('; Code; ...
; physical a..b') give the classified ROM range (file offsets include the 16-byte iNES
; header); 'Static' code is classified from static evidence and may have no known caller
; (noted as lead L-015 where reachability is unresolved; the seven stray returns of lead
; L-016 are unreachable as far as known).  Every byte of the ROM is classified; there are
; no 'Unknown' regions in this map.
; Comments marked tentative are interpretations, not verified facts.
; ---- NES hardware registers (CPU address space) ----
; ---- MMC1 serial registers: writes anywhere in each 8 KiB window; the game uses these exact addresses ----
; reset/serial write to control register ($8000-$9FFF)
; control register window, last address
; CHR bank 0 register window ($A000-$BFFF)
; PRG bank register window ($E000-$FFFF)
; each switchable bank stores its own 16 KiB bank number here
; ---- RAM variables (see comments at each definition) ----
; RAM-SYMBOLS-BEGIN

; iNES header: magic NES<1A>, 16x16KiB PRG, 16x8KiB CHR, mapper 1 (MMC1), horizontal mirroring;
; parsed by romatlas inspect.
; Byte $80 at bank start ($8000/$C000) preceding the reset stub; RESET vector is $8001 so it is
; skipped by execution; identical in all 16 banks.
; Power-on/reset entry (bank 0 is fixed at $8000; every bank begins with a copy of this stub
; so reset works whatever bank MMC1 powers up with).  Disables NMI and rendering, waits for
; the PPU to warm up, silences DMC IRQs, then programs MMC1 control = $0A (vertical
; mirroring, PRG mode 2: bank 0 fixed at $8000 and 16 KiB switchable at $C000, 8 KiB CHR)
; and PRG bank 15.  Clears zero page $20-$55, marks VoiceSample idle ($FF), initialises sound, palette and
; PPU, then falls into MainLoop.
; Main loop (never returns).  When VoiceSample holds a request (not $FF) it runs the
; umpire-voice player (bank 1 entry 0) with NMI disabled, then re-enables NMI.  Between
; tasks it keeps mixing the random state (RandomB ^= RandomA) and services the request
; bits in MainLoopFlags: bit7 LaunchPitchedBall, bit5 AimThrowAtTarget (repeats while set;
; SysFlags bit6 is raised so a concurrent NMI only does sound/split work),
